If essential equipment is absent, list it and stop; do not invent catalog entries or call a partial workflow end to end.

# XChem fragment-screening lab: design run, but 300 crystals/day and a valid layout are not confirmed

I designed and simulated the whole workflow, but it fails two of the three checks. The model did not show 300 crystals/day, and the layout still has 33 overlaps. The only claim that holds is the budget.

| Check (latest design) | Result |
|---|---|
| Median throughput ≥ 300 crystals/day | **Refuted: 0 crystals/day** (low, median and high all 0; 0% chance of meeting target) |
| Equipment cost ≤ USD 2,000,000 | **Supported: USD 988,793** |
| Layout has no violations | **Refuted: 33 overlaps** |

I can't claim this lab is feasible. My two design claims were wrong and I withdraw them.

## Why the simulator shows zero
- **The simulated run is too short.** It covers only 72 hours. One plate takes far longer to get through: about 1.5 days of protein production, about 3 days of crystal growth (my estimate, 1–14 days), soaking, then about 7 days of shipping and beamline queue (3–21 days). No plate reached the final step, so 0 reflects the run length, not the lab's daily capacity. I kept the external shipping and queue step, as you asked, and did not remove it to make the number look better.
- **The simulator may not count crystals.** It moves plates. I assumed about 38 crystals per plate, but I can't tell whether it converts plates into crystals/day.
- **The flagged bottleneck is probably not real.** The starter-culture shaker shows 83% busy. That seems to come from the simulator releasing protein batches nonstop. The design needs only about one protein prep every 2 days. This is my reading of the output, not a tool result.
- **Capacity checks were skipped.** The tool doesn't support them for this design, so there is no steady-state cross-check.

## Layout
- **Run 1:** about 70 overlaps. The automatic placement squeezed everything within reach of a single robot arm.
- **Run 2 (latest):** I removed the arm and had the operators carry plates. Overlaps fell to 33.
- **Still unresolved:** the walk-in cold room, Rock Imager, benches and fume hood still overlap. I can't set positions in the tool.
- **No hazard separation shown:** the separate high-g centrifuge corner and the ventilated cryogen area are stated intentions only. No safety certification is implied.

I stopped after the second run because the 72-hour run limit can't be fixed by changing equipment.

## Equipment (all from the catalog, latest design)
| Stage | Equipment | Cost (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Benches | 2× lab bench | 11,060 |
| Culture | 2× Infors Multitron Pro shaker (2.5 L baffled flasks) | 50,000 |
| Cell harvest and clarification | Beckman Avanti JXN-26 centrifuge | 60,108 |
| Lysis | Qsonica Q700 sonicator | 6,100 |
| Purification | ÄKTA pure 25 (affinity column, then size-exclusion column) | 79,873 |
| Protein check | SDS-PAGE gel kit + NanoDrop | 16,735 |
| Drop setting | mosquito Xtal3 | 95,573 |
| Crystal hotel and imaging | Rock Imager 1000 | 350,000 |
| Cold room | Walk-in cold room (the imager's catalog entry requires one) | 14,144 |
| Fragment soaking | Echo 525 | 246,083 |
| Vibration-free surfaces | 2× TMC vibration table | 12,310 |
| Manual harvesting | 2× Crystal Shifter, one per operator | 26,800 |
| Cryo-cooling and shipping | LN2 dewar + CX100 dry shipper | 3,447 |
| Ventilation | Fume hood | 16,560 |
| **Total** | | **988,793** |

Costs are catalog estimates. Several are rough (Rock Imager USD 250–450k, Echo USD 165–340k, Shifter price is weak). Installation, consumables and building work are excluded.

Nothing essential was missing from the catalog, but three gaps remain:
- **O2 depletion monitor:** not in the catalog. Buy it separately; it is not in the cost total.
- **Dry shipper:** the catalog lists its capacity in vials, not pucks. Puck holders need checking.
- **Consumables:** columns, spin concentrators, crystallisation plates, the fragment library, loops/pins, UniPucks and liquid nitrogen are not costed.

## Assumptions (my estimates; no literature was available)
The literature search wasn't set up (API key missing), so nothing here is cited.
- **Protein yield:** 10 mg/L (range 1–50). One prep is 4 × 1 L cultures, about 40 mg (4–200 mg).
- **Protein use:** about 0.2–0.5 mg per plate, so one prep feeds 16 plates. Below about 2 mg/L that breaks down.
- **Crystal success:** 50% of drops give a usable crystal (20–90%), and 80% survive soaking and harvesting (50–95%). That is about 38 crystals per plate (10–82).
- **Plates needed:** about 8 per day to reach 300 crystals/day (anywhere from about 4 to 30 given the ranges above).
- **Harvest time:** about 60 s per crystal (20–120 s), so about 2,280 s per plate. The two operators are assumed to share a day shift (16 operator-hours a day).
- **Rough hand calculation (not simulated):** 8 plates/day of harvesting is about 5 operator-hours. Protein work adds roughly 4 hours a day on average. That fits within 16 operator-hours, but harvesting will probably be the real limit, as is usual for XChem-style work. The simulator didn't confirm this.

## Next steps
1. **Simulate longer or start full.** Run at least 2–3 weeks, or start with crystal plates and protein batches already in progress, then rerun the checks.
2. **Fix the room layout.** Draw zones by hand, with the cold room and imager on one wall, the high-g corner and the ventilated cryogen area separate, and enter fixed positions if the tool allows.
3. **Count crystals directly.** Confirm the simulator counts crystals, or switch the target to about 8 plates/day using the stated conversion.
4. **Replace my estimates with real numbers.** Measure protein yield and crystal success with a pilot study, or get literature access, before relying on these figures.

The generated report matches this summary, including both withdrawn claims.

lab_spec.name: XChem-style fragment screening by crystallography
lab_spec.description: Express a soluble E. coli target protein, harvest cells, lyse/clarify, purify, QC/concentrate, set crystallisation drops, grow and image crystals, select drops, soak fragments, manually harvest crystals, cryo-cool/load pucks and ship to an external synchrotron for diffraction, then in-silico hit analysis. No in-house X-ray. Target 300 crystals/day steady state in a 10 m x 8 m room, USD 2,000,000 equipment budget, instruments 24 h/day, two skilled operators on 8 h shifts. BSL1; high-g centrifuges and cryogens need separated work areas, ventilation and O2 monitoring.
notes: Revision 2: UR5e removed; operators carry plates (about 8 plates/day) to avoid arm-reach packing.
Flow unit downstream of protein QC = one 96-well 3-subwell sitting-drop crystallisation plate (SWISSCI-type); 1 drop per well soaked.

ASSUMPTION (agent_estimate): usable crystals per plate = 96 drops x 0.5 drops with a soakable crystal (range 0.2-0.9) x 0.8 soak/harvest survival (range 0.5-0.95) = ~38 mounted crystals per plate (range ~10-82). 300 crystals/day therefore needs ~8 plates/day (range ~3.7-30).

ASSUMPTION (agent_estimate): purified protein yield 10 mg/L E. coli culture (range 1-50 mg/L); one prep = 4 x 2.5 L baffled flasks with 1 L each = ~40 mg (4-200 mg). Consumption ~0.2-0.5 mg per plate, so one prep feeds 16 plates (~3-8 mg) with margin unless yield is below ~2 mg/L.
Operators assumed to work an overlapping day shift (16 operator-hours/day); unattended instruments run 24 h.

Zoning intent: centrifuge in a separated high-g corner with clearance; LN2 dewar, Crystal Shifters and cryo bench in a separated, ventilated cryogen area with an O2 depletion monitor (O2 monitor not in catalog, procure separately, not in BOM).
Consumables not in BOM: IMAC and SEC columns, spin concentrators, crystallisation plates, fragment library source plates, loops/pins, UniPucks, LN2 supply.
